Thermonuclear

Type Ia explosions disrupt a carbon–oxygen white dwarf. Their light curves are comparatively uniform, so calibrated Type Ia events act as standardisable candles—not perfectly identical candles.

Radioactive powering

The luminosity is commonly linked to the decay chain 56Ni → 56Co → 56Fe. As ejecta expand, energy deposition and photon escape shape the decline.

Core collapse

Type II events retain hydrogen. In Type II-P, hydrogen recombination creates a broad plateau; II-L declines more continuously, while IIn adds a simplified interaction-powered component.

Teaching model only: real light curves depend on ejecta mass, composition, nickel yield, mixing, opacity, geometry, viewing band and circumstellar material.
